title: Regrets and Alternatives
description: Speculate about the past and its consequences using the third conditional, mixed conditionals and conditional expressions without if (unless, provided that, as long as, supposing, otherwise). Vocabulary: decisions, turning points and luck.
objectives: Use the third conditional to talk about imaginary past situations
Use mixed conditionals to link past and present
Express conditions with unless, provided that, as long as, supposing and otherwise
Talk about decisions, turning points and luck with natural vocabulary

lessons.title: Third Conditional: Imagining a Different Past
lessons.summary: Menggunakan third conditional untuk membayangkan masa lalu yang berbeda dan akibatnya.
objectives: Form the third conditional (if + past perfect, would have + past participle)
Use could have and might have in the result clause
Understand contracted forms such as If I'd known, I'd have...
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Meaning
The third conditional describes an **imaginary past**: something that did *not* happen, and its imaginary result. Because the past cannot change, these sentences often express **regret**, **relief** or **criticism**.
- *If we **had left** earlier, we **wouldn't have missed** the train.* (Reality: we left late and missed it.)

### Form
| If-clause | Result clause |
| --- | --- |
| if + **past perfect** (had + past participle) | **would have** + past participle |
| If I **had known** about the party, | I **would have come**. |
| If she **hadn't helped** me, | I **would have failed**. |

The clauses can change places. Use a comma only when the if-clause comes first: *I would have come if I had known.*

### Other modals in the result clause
| Modal | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| would have | certain result | *We would have won.* |
| could have | possible / able | *We could have won* (it was possible). |
| might have | perhaps | *We might have won* (maybe). |

### Contractions — be careful with 'd
In speech, both *had* and *would* become **'d**:
- *If I**'d** (had) known, I**'d** (would) have come.*

Tip: after *if*, 'd = **had**; before *have*, 'd = **would**.

### Questions and negatives
- *What **would** you **have done** if you **had lost** your passport?*
- *If he **hadn't been** so tired, he **wouldn't have made** that mistake.*

### Common errors
- ✗ *If I would have known...* → never use *would have* in the if-clause.
- ✗ *If I knew yesterday, I would come.* → for the past, use the past perfect and *would have*.

> **Catatan:** Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita memakai *seandainya/kalau saja ... (dulu)*, dan kata kerja tidak berubah. Dalam bahasa Inggris, situasi masa lalu yang tidak nyata **harus** memakai **had + V3** di klausa if dan **would have + V3** di klausa hasil. Contoh: *Seandainya saya tahu, saya pasti datang* → *If I had known, I would have come.*

lessons.title: Mixed Conditionals: Linking Past and Present
lessons.summary: Menghubungkan masa lalu dan masa kini dengan mixed conditionals.
objectives: Use a past condition with a present result (if + past perfect, would + infinitive)
Use a present condition with a past result (if + past simple, would have + past participle)
Choose between second, third and mixed conditionals from the context
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Why mix?
Real life doesn't always stay in one time frame. A past event can affect the present, and a permanent present situation can explain a past event. Mixed conditionals combine parts of the **second** and **third** conditionals.

### Type A: past condition → present result
| If-clause (past) | Result (now) |
| --- | --- |
| if + **past perfect** | **would/could/might + infinitive** |
| If I **had taken** that job in Singapore, | I **would live** there now. |
| If she **hadn't missed** the flight, | she **would be** in Rome now. |

Typical signals in the result: *now, today, still, at the moment*.

### Type B: present (general) condition → past result
| If-clause (always/now) | Result (past) |
| --- | --- |
| if + **past simple** | **would have + past participle** |
| If I **were** more organised, | I **wouldn't have missed** the deadline yesterday. |
| If he **spoke** Spanish, | he **would have got** the job in Madrid. |

Here the if-clause describes a permanent quality or situation (*be organised, speak Spanish*), not a single past event.

### Choosing the right conditional
Ask two questions:
1. **When** is the condition? (past event or general/present fact?)
2. **When** is the result? (past or now?)

| Condition | Result | Conditional |
| --- | --- | --- |
| present/unreal | present | second: *If I had time, I'd help.* |
| past | past | third: *If I'd had time, I'd have helped.* |
| past | present | mixed A: *If I'd slept, I wouldn't be tired now.* |
| present | past | mixed B: *If I weren't so shy, I'd have spoken to her.* |

### Continuous forms
The result can be continuous: *If I hadn't lost my job, I **would be working** in the city now.*

> **Catatan:** Kunci mixed conditional adalah **kata keterangan waktu**. Jika ada *now/sekarang* di hasil, pakai *would + V1*; jika kondisinya sifat permanen (*seandainya saya orangnya lebih rapi*), pakai *past simple* di klausa if. Gunakan *were* untuk semua subjek dalam gaya formal: *If I were...*

sections.summary: Mixed conditionals link time frames: **If + past perfect → would + infinitive (now)** for past causes of present results, and **If + past simple → would have + past participle** for permanent qualities that explain past results. Check the time of the condition and of the result. *Ringkasan: perhatikan kata waktu seperti now, yesterday, last year.*

lessons.title: Conditions Without If
lessons.summary: Mengungkapkan syarat tanpa kata if: unless, provided that, as long as, supposing, otherwise.
objectives: Use unless to mean except if
Use provided/providing (that) and as long as for strong conditions
Use supposing and otherwise to imagine situations and give consequences
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Alternatives to if
At B2 level you can make your conditions more precise with other words.

| Word | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unless | except if / if ... not | We'll go **unless** it rains. |
| provided (that) / providing (that) | only if (strong condition) | You can borrow the car **provided that** you fill it up. |
| as long as / so long as | only if (more informal) | I'll come **as long as** I can leave early. |
| on condition that | only if (formal) | He was released **on condition that** he paid a fine. |
| supposing / suppose | imagine that | **Supposing** you lost your job, what would you do? |
| otherwise | if not (refers to the previous sentence) | Hurry up; **otherwise**, we'll be late. |

### unless
*Unless* already contains a negative idea, so don't use another negative in the same clause:
- ✓ *You won't pass **unless** you **study**.* (= if you don't study)
- ✗ *You won't pass unless you don't study.*

### provided that / as long as
These stress that the condition is necessary. Use present tenses for future meaning:
- *I'll lend you the money **as long as** you **pay** me back next month.* (NOT *will pay*)

### supposing
*Supposing* can introduce real or unreal situations and is often used in questions:
- *Supposing it **rains** tomorrow — shall we cancel?* (real possibility)
- *Supposing you **had** a million dollars, what **would** you do?* (unreal)
- *Supposing you **had failed**, what **would** you **have done**?* (past)

### otherwise
*Otherwise* links two sentences or clauses. It usually follows a full stop or semicolon, or *and/or*:
- *Take an umbrella. **Otherwise**, you'll get soaked.*
- *I had my phone with me; **otherwise**, I would have been completely lost.*

### in case is different!
*In case* is **not** a conditional; it means 'as a precaution':
- *Take an umbrella **in case** it rains.* (Take it now because it might rain.)
- *Take an umbrella **if** it rains.* (Only take it if it is raining.)

> **Catatan:** *unless* = *kecuali jika*; *provided that / as long as* = *asalkan*; *supposing* = *andaikan*; *otherwise* = *kalau tidak / jika tidak begitu*; *in case* = *untuk berjaga-jaga*. Kesalahan umum: *unless ... don't* (negatif ganda).

examples.en: We'll have the barbecue in the garden unless it rains.
examples.id: Kami akan mengadakan barbekyu di taman kecuali jika hujan.

examples.id: Kamu boleh memakai laptopku asalkan kamu tidak menginstal apa pun.

examples.en: I wrote the address down; otherwise, I would have forgotten it.
examples.id: Saya mencatat alamatnya; kalau tidak, saya pasti sudah lupa.

vocabulary.example: Don't call me unless it's urgent.
Provided that the weather is good, we'll sail.
Supposing you won, what would you buy?

grammar.pattern: result + unless + positive clause (present for future)
grammar.example: I'll be there unless my train is late.

grammar.pattern: result + provided (that) / as long as + present simple
grammar.example: You'll be fine as long as you stay calm.
Write it down. Otherwise, you'll forget it.

mistakes.wrong: Unless you don't hurry, you'll miss the bus.
mistakes.right: Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus.
mistakes.why: Unless already means if ... not, so don't add another negative.

mistakes.wrong: You can come provided that you will bring some food.
mistakes.right: You can come provided that you bring some food.
mistakes.why: Use the present simple after provided that for future meaning.

mistakes.wrong: Take an umbrella if it rains later.
mistakes.right: Take an umbrella in case it rains later.
mistakes.why: For a precaution (just in case), use in case, not if.

sections.summary: Use **unless** (= if not), **provided that / as long as** (= only if), **supposing** (= imagine), and **otherwise** (= if not, referring back) to express conditions precisely. Use present tenses for future meaning after these words, and avoid double negatives with *unless*. *Ringkasan: unless = kecuali jika; provided that = asalkan; otherwise = kalau tidak.*

reviewCards.back: kecuali jika (= if ... not); no double negative
kalau tidak (refers to the previous sentence)
in case = sebagai antisipasi; if = hanya jika terjadi

answers: You won't get a table unless you book in advance.
You will not get a table unless you book in advance.
questions.explanation: *If you don't book* = **unless you book**. Do not add another negative after *unless*.

questions.prompt: Complete with ONE word.

answers: Otherwise

questions.prompt: Find the error.
questions.explanation: *Unless* already has a negative meaning, so: **Unless you hurry, you'll miss the last bus.**

questions.prompt: Which sentence means the same as: 'You can borrow my bike, but only if you bring it back by six.'?
options: You can borrow my bike provided that you bring it back by six.
You can borrow my bike unless you bring it back by six.
You can borrow my bike in case you bring it back by six.
You can borrow my bike otherwise you bring it back by six.
questions.explanation: *Only if* = **provided that** (asalkan). *Unless* reverses the meaning, *in case* means 'as a precaution', and *otherwise* cannot be used like this.

questions.prompt: Choose the most logical reply.

dialogue.speaker: Fajar
dialogue.text: I'm thinking of quitting my job to open a café.

options: Supposing it doesn't work out, what will you do?
Supposing it doesn't work out, what did you do?
Unless it works out, you'll definitely be rich.
Provided that it fails, you'll be fine.
questions.explanation: **Supposing** introduces an imagined possibility, followed by a logical question about the future. Option 2 uses the wrong tense, and options 3 and 4 don't make sense.

lessons.title: Vocabulary: Decisions, Turning Points and Luck
lessons.summary: Kosakata dan ungkapan tentang keputusan, titik balik, dan keberuntungan.
objectives: Use vocabulary for making decisions (weigh up, have second thoughts)
Talk about turning points and missed opportunities
Use expressions for luck and chance (by chance, a stroke of luck, a narrow escape)
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Making decisions
| Expression | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| weigh up (the pros and cons) | consider advantages and disadvantages | She **weighed up** the pros and cons before moving. |
| on the spur of the moment | suddenly, without planning | We booked the trip **on the spur of the moment**. |
| have second thoughts (about) | start to doubt a decision | I'm **having second thoughts** about the course. |
| make up your mind | decide | Have you **made up your mind** yet? |
| take a risk / take a chance | do something that might fail | He **took a risk** and started his own company. |

### Turning points
| Expression | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| a turning point | a moment when things change direction |
| a missed opportunity | a good chance that was not used |
| in hindsight / with hindsight | when you look back with present knowledge |
| it changed my life | had a major effect |

*Moving to Surabaya was a **turning point** in my career. **In hindsight**, refusing the scholarship was a **missed opportunity**.*

### Luck and chance
| Expression | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| by chance / by accident | not planned |
| a stroke of luck | a sudden piece of good luck |
| a narrow escape | a situation where you almost had an accident or problem |
| (un)fortunately | (sadly) luckily |
| it was meant to be | fate wanted it to happen |

### Using the vocabulary with conditionals
These expressions often appear together with the grammar of this unit:
- *If I hadn't met Lia **by chance**, I wouldn't be working here now.*
- *It was **a stroke of luck** that the taxi came; **otherwise**, we would have missed the flight.*
- ***In hindsight**, I would have **weighed up** the options more carefully.*

### Collocation tips
- **make** a decision (NOT *do a decision*); **take** a risk/chance
- **by** chance, **by** accident (NOT *with chance*)
- **in** hindsight

> **Catatan:** *Take a chance* = mengambil risiko/kesempatan; *by chance* = secara kebetulan. *Second thoughts* = mulai ragu atas keputusan; selalu jamak (*thoughts*). *A narrow escape* = nyaris celaka/terhindar.

examples.id: Kalau dipikir sekarang, menolak tawaran itu adalah kesempatan yang terlewatkan.

examples.id: Kami bertemu secara kebetulan di halte bus di Malang.

grammar.pattern: In hindsight, + clause (often with would have + past participle)
grammar.example: In hindsight, I would have chosen a different course.

mistakes.right: I had second thoughts about the trip.
mistakes.why: The expression is plural: have second thoughts.

sections.summary: Talk about decisions with **weigh up, make up your mind, take a risk, have second thoughts, on the spur of the moment**; about change with **turning point, missed opportunity, in hindsight**; and about luck with **by chance, a stroke of luck, a narrow escape**. Combine them with conditionals to tell stories. *Ringkasan: pelajari ungkapan sebagai satu kesatuan.*

reviewCards.front: on the spur of the moment

questions.prompt: Choose the expression that best completes the sentence.
questions.instructions: Hint: the moment when everything changed direction.
questions.context: Moving to Bandung was a ___ in my life: from that moment, my career went in a completely new direction.
options: turning point
narrow escape
second thought
spur of the moment
questions.explanation: A **turning point** is a moment when things change direction (titik balik). A *narrow escape* is almost having an accident; *second thoughts* are doubts (and always plural); *spur of the moment* means spontaneous.

questions.prompt: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.right: a sudden piece of good fortune
a situation where you almost had an accident
looking back with what you know now

questions.explanation: These expressions are common when telling stories about decisions and luck. Learn them as complete chunks.

questions.prompt: Complete the phrasal verb with ONE word.
questions.text: Before you accept the offer, you should weigh ___ the pros and cons.
answers: up
questions.explanation: **Weigh up** = consider carefully (menimbang-nimbang).

questions.prompt: Complete the story with words from the bank.
questions.text: I bought the flat on the spur of the ___, without thinking much. In ___, it wasn't a wise decision, because I hadn't checked the costs. But by a stroke of ___, its value has since doubled.
answers: moment
hindsight
luck
questions.explanation: Fixed phrases: **on the spur of the moment**, **in hindsight**, **a stroke of luck**.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses 'by chance' correctly?
options: I met my business partner completely by chance on a train.
I took a big by chance when I left my job.
She had by chance thoughts about the trip.
By chance is very important in business.
questions.explanation: **By chance** is an adverbial phrase meaning 'without planning' (secara kebetulan): *I met my business partner by chance.*

questions.prompt: Translate into English.
questions.source: Saya bertemu istri saya secara kebetulan.
answers: I met my wife by chance.
I met my wife by accident.
I met my wife purely by chance.
I met my wife completely by chance.
I happened to meet my wife.
questions.explanation: *Secara kebetulan* = **by chance** (or *by accident*). The verb *meet* is in the past simple: *met*.

lessons.title: Talking About Turning Points
lessons.summary: Berspekulasi tentang masa lalu dan akibatnya dengan if it hadn't been for, inversi formal, dan conditional campuran.
objectives: Use If it hadn't been for... to show what made a difference
Recognise the formal inversion Had I known...
Tell a story about a turning point using third and mixed conditionals
lessons.completionCriteria: Complete the writing task and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Selesaikan tugas menulis dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Showing what made the difference
**If it hadn't been for + noun** means 'without this person/thing':
- *If it hadn't been for my teacher's encouragement, I would never have applied.*
- *If it hadn't been for the rain, we would have won.*

For a present situation, use **If it weren't for**: *If it weren't for my sister, I'd be lonely here.*

**But for + noun** is a more formal alternative: *But for your help, we would have failed.*

### Formal inversion (no if)
In formal writing, you can drop *if* and put *had* first:
| Normal | Inverted (formal) |
| --- | --- |
| If I had known about the traffic, | **Had I known** about the traffic, |
| If she hadn't called, | **Had she not called**, |

Note the negative: *Had she not called* (NOT *Hadn't she called*).

### Telling a turning-point story
A good story about a life-changing moment usually has:
1. **Background** (past simple/continuous, past perfect): *In 2018, I was working in a bank and I had never thought about teaching.*
2. **The moment** (past simple): *One day, a friend asked me to help at her school.*
3. **The alternative past** (third conditional): *If she hadn't asked me, I would have stayed in banking.*
4. **The present result** (mixed conditional): *If I hadn't said yes, I wouldn't be a teacher now.*
5. **Reflection**: *In hindsight, it was the best decision I've ever made.*

### Useful phrases
| Purpose | Phrase |
| --- | --- |
| looking back | *Looking back, ... / In hindsight, ...* |
| alternative outcome | *Things might have turned out very differently.* |
| luck | *It was pure luck that... / Fortunately, ...* |
| present effect | *That's why I'm ... now.* |

> **Catatan:** *If it hadn't been for* = *seandainya tidak ada / kalau bukan karena* (masa lalu). Inversi *Had I known* bersifat formal, cocok untuk esai atau surat resmi; dalam percakapan sehari-hari *If I had known* lebih umum.

examples.en: If it hadn't been for my teacher's encouragement, I would never have applied for the scholarship.
examples.id: Kalau bukan karena dorongan guru saya, saya tidak akan pernah mendaftar beasiswa itu.
examples.note: If it hadn't been for + noun

examples.en: Had I known about the strike, I would have taken a taxi.
examples.id: Seandainya saya tahu tentang mogok itu, saya akan naik taksi.

examples.en: If I hadn't missed that bus, I would never have met my business partner.
examples.id: Seandainya saya tidak ketinggalan bus itu, saya tidak akan pernah bertemu rekan bisnis saya.

examples.en: Looking back, things might have turned out very differently.
examples.id: Kalau dipikir lagi, semuanya bisa saja berakhir sangat berbeda.

vocabulary.example: Her encouragement made all the difference.
Everything turned out well in the end.
She won a scholarship to study in Leeds.
A good mentor can make all the difference.
Looking back, I'm glad I took the risk.

grammar.pattern: If it hadn't been for + noun, subject + would (not) have + past participle
grammar.example: If it hadn't been for the map, we would have got lost.

grammar.pattern: If it weren't for + noun, subject + would + infinitive
grammar.example: If it weren't for my job, I'd travel more.

grammar.pattern: Had + subject (+ not) + past participle, subject + would have + past participle
grammar.example: Had we not left early, we would have missed the ferry.

mistakes.wrong: If it wasn't been for you, I would have failed.
mistakes.right: If it hadn't been for you, I would have failed.
mistakes.why: For the past, the fixed form is If it hadn't been for.

mistakes.wrong: Hadn't she called, we would have left.
mistakes.right: Had she not called, we would have left.
mistakes.why: In inverted conditionals, the negative is Had + subject + not.

mistakes.wrong: Had I know the truth, I would have told you.
mistakes.right: Had I known the truth, I would have told you.
mistakes.why: Inversion still needs the past participle (known).

sections.summary: Use **If it hadn't been for / But for + noun** to show what made the difference, and **Had I known...** (formal inversion) instead of *If I had known*. A turning-point story combines background, the key moment, the alternative past (third conditional), the present result (mixed conditional) and a reflection. *Ringkasan: ceritakan apa yang terjadi, apa yang mungkin terjadi, dan akibatnya sekarang.*

reviewCards.back: Formal inversion = If I had known, ...

reviewCards.front: Had she not called (not: Hadn't she called)

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the missing word(s).
questions.instructions: Hint: the fixed phrase is If it ___ been for...
questions.text: If it ___ been for my teacher's encouragement, I would never have applied for the scholarship.
answers: hadn't
had not
questions.explanation: **If it hadn't been for + noun** = without this person/thing (in the past).

questions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so that it means the same.
questions.sentence: I only passed the exam because my friend helped me.
questions.cue: Begin with: If it hadn't been for ...
answers: If it hadn't been for my friend's help, I wouldn't have passed the exam.
If it hadn't been for my friend, I wouldn't have passed the exam.
If it hadn't been for my friend's help, I would not have passed the exam.
If it hadn't been for my friend, I would not have passed the exam.
If it hadn't been for my friend's help, I would have failed the exam.
If it hadn't been for my friend, I would have failed the exam.
If it hadn't been for my friend's help, I wouldn't have passed.
If it hadn't been for my friend, I wouldn't have passed.
questions.explanation: *Only ... because my friend helped me* → **If it hadn't been for my friend('s help), I wouldn't have passed the exam.**

questions.prompt: Write about a turning point in your life or in the life of someone you know (120–180 words). Describe the background, the key moment, what would have happened otherwise (third conditional), how it affects the present (mixed conditional) and your reflection.
questions.explanation: Use the five-part structure from the lesson. Include at least one third conditional, one mixed conditional and one expression such as *in hindsight* or *if it hadn't been for*.

questions.prompt: Put the fragments in the correct order.
fragments: if I hadn't missed that bus,
questions.explanation: Reflection phrase → if-clause (past perfect) → result (would never have + past participle) → relative clause.

questions.prompt: Complete the formal sentence.
questions.text: Had I ___ about the traffic, I ___ earlier.
questions.explanation: Inversion: **Had I known** = If I had known; result: **would have left**.

questions.prompt: Which sentence describes a past condition with a PRESENT result?
options: If I hadn't broken my leg, I would be playing in the final today.
If I hadn't broken my leg, I would have played in the final yesterday.
If I break my leg, I won't play in the final.
If I broke my leg, I wouldn't play in the final.
questions.explanation: *Hadn't broken* (past condition) + *would be playing today* (present result) = mixed conditional. Option 2 is a third conditional; options 3 and 4 are first and second conditionals.

unitTestQuestions.context: The fire alarm went off at 3 a.m., and everyone woke up and left the hotel safely.
unitTestQuestions.text: If the alarm ___ off, nobody would have woken up in time.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Third conditional if-clause for an imaginary past: **hadn't gone off** (+ would have woken up).

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Rewrite the situation as a conditional sentence.
unitTestQuestions.sentence: We got lost because we didn't have a map.
unitTestQuestions.cue: Begin with: If we had had ...
answers: If we had had a map, we wouldn't have got lost.
If we had had a map, we would not have got lost.
If we had had a map, we wouldn't have gotten lost.
If we had had a map, we would not have gotten lost.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Had had* = past perfect of *have*. Reverse both facts: **If we had had a map, we wouldn't have got lost.**

unitTestQuestions.context: I'll lend you the money ___ you pay me back by the end of next month.
options: provided that
unless
otherwise
in case
unitTestQuestions.explanation: The lending depends on a condition → **provided that** (asalkan). *Unless* would reverse the meaning.
Never use *would have* in the if-clause: **If I had known about the party, I would have come.**

unitTestQuestions.source: Seandainya Dewi tidak kehilangan paspornya, dia pasti sudah berada di Paris sekarang.
answers: If Dewi hadn't lost her passport, she would be in Paris now.
If Dewi had not lost her passport, she would be in Paris now.
If Dewi hadn't lost her passport, she'd be in Paris now.
If Dewi hadn't lost her passport, she would already be in Paris now.
If Dewi hadn't lost her passport, she would definitely be in Paris now.
If Dewi hadn't lost her passport, she would certainly be in Paris now.
If Dewi hadn't lost her passport, she would be in Paris by now.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Past condition (losing the passport) + present result (*sekarang*) → mixed conditional: **If Dewi hadn't lost her passport, she would be in Paris now.**

pairs.right: we'll have the picnic in the park.
as long as you text me.

unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Unless* = if not; *supposing* = imagine; *otherwise* = if you don't; *as long as* = only if.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: What does the phrase in bold mean?
unitTestQuestions.context: I signed up for the course, but now I'm **having second thoughts** because it's so expensive.
options: starting to doubt my decision
thinking twice as fast
feeling very excited
planning a second course
unitTestQuestions.explanation: **Have second thoughts** = start to doubt a decision you have made (mulai ragu).
